label: token c fed back as input early in the copy phase (2nd/3rd copy step)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is c (100% of activations have in_tok=c), almost entirely at recall_idx 1-2, i.e. when the fed-back c is original token 0 or 1. recall_idx 2 (c was original token 1, e.g. a c ... <DEL> a [c]) holds about 76% of the mass and gives the strongest activations. recall_idx 1 (c was the first token) holds about 23% and is weaker. A small tail sits at recall_idx 3. Magnitude is larger for longer sequences (more outputs still to go). Many c inputs at recall_idx 1-2 in short sequences (L of 4-5) stay silent, which caps precision at about 0.66. Never fires in the original phase, on <DEL>, on any other token, or on c later in the copy phase. Adding L conditions (e.g. recall_idx 2 with L>=5, or recall_idx 1 with L>=6) only raises F1 to about 0.80.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=10: c; t=9: c; t=11: c) and the third original token (most: 3, l, v, h, x, i; least: j, 0, w, e); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, recall_idx=1, L=3 & t=4.
